lemma: Reuse-elimination (naive): for an acyclic De Morgan circuit C with S non-input gates and r gates of fan-out >= 2, f_C has a De Morgan formula with at most 2^r * 2S leaves. Proof: order the reused gates topologically; for b in {0,1}^r let term_b = AND_j [g_j(x,b)=b_j] AND [out(x,b)=1], where reused gates are read as constants b. Least-index argument: if b != y(x) (true values), the least j with b_j != y_j(x) fails its check, since g_j reads only inputs with index < j, which agree with y. So exactly one term is consistent and OR_b term_b = f_C. Each term is a fan-out-1 forest with <= 2S leaves (x-literals), so the total is <= 2^r * 2S.
gap: This gives exponent 2^r, not S(r+1)^c with c<1, so it does not advance R-MCSP. The earlier Lean statement (claim:3db94b5537c2) was FIDELITY_REJECTED because it was over an abstract type Fm; the circuit-level statement is not formalized. No MCSP-specific lemma yet; the locality filter F2 is not checked; the controls EQ, IP and MUX are not run.

evidence: Reviewed by R0728 (did not claim S0001). Hand argument: take reused set R (non-output gates of fan-out >= 2), r = |R|. For b in {0,1}^R, term_b = AND over g in R of [gate g computed from inputs and reused gates h<g set to b_h equals b_g] AND [output computed with R set to b equals 1]. OR_b term_b = f_C: if f(x)=1 take b = actual values of R (checks pass by induction on index); conversely a passing term forces b = actual values, so output = f(x). Leaf count per term: non-reused gates have fan-out 1, so each lies in exactly one tree (the tree of its parent reused gate or the output); reused gates are roots of their own trees and cut elsewhere; so the r+1 trees have at most S internal gates in total and at most S + r + 1 input leaves. Hence per-term leaves <= S + r + 1 <= 2S for S >= r+1 (true, since R and out are gates), and L <= 2^r (S + r + 1) <= 2^r * 2S. Exact check cm-fba47b5731644c70: 400 random acyclic De Morgan circuits, n<=4, S<=8, bad_equalities=0, per_term_over_2S=0, worst ratio 1.0. Scope limits: the claim needs the output to be a gate (S >= 1); with S=0 and an input-literal output the bound 2^0 * 0 = 0 fails, so the hypothesis S>=1 must be stated. The validator's objection (cm-4bb50ea936c041c4: full tree unfolding U=22962 > 20992 on the chain family at d>=9) refutes a different count (unfolding the whole circuit with no cutting), not this per-term count.

proved_step: Inclusion-exclusion identity: for any CNF F = C_1 and ... and C_m on n variables, #SAT(F) = sum over subsets S of clauses of (-1)^|S| N(S), where N(S) = #{x in {0,1}^n : x falsifies every clause in S} = 2^(n-|V(S)|) if the literals forced by S are consistent, and 0 otherwise. Proof: [x satisfies F] = prod_i (1 - [x falsifies C_i]); expanding the product gives the sum over S, and the S-term counts x falsifying all of S.

evidence: Independent review (session not R0778). Hand check: [x satisfies F] = prod_i (1 - [x falsifies C_i]); expanding gives sum over clause subsets S of (-1)^|S| N(S), N(S) = #{x falsifying all clauses in S}. Falsifying literal (v,s) forces x_v = 1-s, so N(S) = 0 if S forces some variable both ways and 2^(n-|V(S)|) otherwise; the empty S gives 2^n. Exact check cm-8767fb240eae4246: 11702 exhaustive CNFs (n<=3, m<=3, all clause sets of size 1..n over both polarities) plus 2000 random n=4 CNFs with repeated and opposite-polarity literals, 0 mismatches. Scope: the identity is general (any CNF on n variables); the computer check covers only the listed small cases, so the general claim rests on the hand proof. Survives review; it does not advance the reuse-elimination gap (exponent 2^r, no c<1 bound), which stays open.

Attack 2, hand argument: [x satisfies F] = prod_i (1 - [x falsifies C_i]); expanding gives sum over S of (-1)^|S| [x falsifies every clause in S]; summing over x gives N(S). Empty clause: falsified by every x; the expansion still gives #SAT=0 for F containing it, since the terms pair off. Tautology (x or not x): falsifying it needs x=0 and x=1, so N(S)=0, detected by the consistency check. Repeated literals merge into one forced value. No gap found by hand. Scope: general argument plus finite check; not Lean-checked.

proved_step:
LEMMA (De Morgan leaf size, general). Setting: formulas are trees with fan-in-2 gates from {AND, OR} and leaves labelled by literals x_i or NOT x_i; L(f) = minimum number of leaves over formulas computing f. Parity_d(x) = x_1 XOR ... XOR x_d.
(A) L(NOT f) = L(f). Proof: for a formula F, let F^d be obtained by swapping AND and OR at every gate and negating every leaf literal. By induction on F, F^d computes NOT of F's function (De Morgan), and F^d has the same number of leaves. Hence L(NOT f) <= L(f), and the reverse follows by applying the same argument to NOT f.
(B) L(f XOR g) <= 2(L(f) + L(g)). Proof: take formulas F, G with leaves L(f), L(g). By (A), F^d and G^d compute NOT f and NOT g with the same leaf counts. The formula H = (F AND G^d) OR (F^d AND G) computes (f AND NOT g) OR (NOT f AND g) = f XOR g and has 2L(f) + 2L(g) leaves (F, F^d, G, G^d are each a copy of a subtree).
(C) For every j >= 0, L(parity_{2^j}) <= 4^j. Proof by induction. j = 0: parity_1 = x_1, one leaf, 1 = 4^0. Step: parity_{2^{j+1}}(x) = parity_{2^j}(x_left) XOR parity_{2^j}(x_right) on disjoint variable sets. By (B), L <= 2(4^j + 4^j) = 4^{j+1}. Since parity_{2^j} is computed by a formula on 2^j variables with 4^j = (2^j)^2 leaves, this gives the exact pattern d^2 at d = 2^j.
NOTE (not a claim): the same recursion for general d gives L(parity_6) <= 2(L(3)+L(3)) = 40 > 36 = 6^2 with L(3)=10, so the bound d^2 is NOT derived for general d by this construction; only the powers of two are proved.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE: nothing about DAGs with reuse, constant-width state, or the S0001 conversion lemma (a reused DAG of size S with shared state -> formula of size poly(S)). S0001 stays REFUTED-as-stated / OPEN.
